clue.text: Good opening song for Broadway show

indicators.note: the word for good splits open the song, sitting within it

parts.note: a carol is a song, especially a Christmas one
use is worth or good, as in 'is it any use?'

explanation.surface: A cheerful number chosen to start a Broadway musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good' here is a noun-like sense, as in 'it's no good' meaning 'it's no use'; 'opening' tells us it splits the song.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical first staged on Broadway in 1945.

clue.text: What Frasier must pay for a geranium?

definitions.text: What Frasier must pay for a geranium?

parts.words: What Frasier must pay for a geranium?
parts.note: Frasier's surname is Crane, so his invoice is that surname plus 's and an account; the plant is named the same way

explanation.walkthrough: Frasier Crane is the psychiatrist of the US sitcom Frasier; the question asks for the account he owes, which spells a plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranesbill is the common name for hardy Geranium plants, named for their beak-shaped seed pods.

clue.text: Tank on banks of Seine river to see in Paris

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: the banks are the two edges of the word, its outer letters

parts.note: its first and last letters
R is the map abbreviation for river
voir is French for to see

explanation.surface: A tank stationed on the Seine's banks, where Parisians go to look at the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a storage tank or basin holding a supply of water.

clue.text: Turmoil for Putin, a man rarely wrong politically

indicators.note: turmoil is disorder, so the letters of the following words are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: Chaos in the Kremlin, caused by a man whose behaviour is seldom politically incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: Unparliamentary language is improper in parliamentary debate, hence wrong in a political setting.

clue.text: Old England manager has lost five licences

indicators.note: the manager's name drops the numeral, losing it

parts.note: Terry Venables managed the England football team from 1994 to 1996
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A former England football boss has been stripped of five permits.
explanation.definitionFit: To license someone is to authorise or permit them, just as to enable them is.

clue.text: On date with a hairy pig

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig with a bristly coat

explanation.surface: Someone has gone on a date with a rather hairy, pig-like companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on a ship, train or other vehicle, as in passengers on or aboard.

clue.text: Helpful person's reorganised random sailor's property

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, helpful person; with the 's it gives the plural form

indicators.note: reorganising the word random puts its letters in a new order

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A kind person's belongings are rearranged at random, alongside a sailor's goods.
explanation.walkthrough: A brick is British slang for a dependable, helpful person; tar is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricks and mortar is a phrase for buildings or real estate, a form of property.

clue.text: Respond to current fashion

parts.note: AC is alternating current
ton is an old word for high fashion, as in 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: Advice to keep up by reacting to the latest trends.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on a suggestion is to take action in response to it.

clue.text: Fight expected close to school

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at noon

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A playground brawl is anticipated near the school gates.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal combat between two people, a kind of fight.

clue.text: Short run then good jump

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a sprint is a fast run

explanation.surface: An athlete's brief dash followed by a fine leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to leap or bound suddenly upward or forward.

clue.text: Moralist has bagels regularly before work

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A preachy type eats bagels routinely before heading to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek fabulist whose tales each end with a moral lesson.

clue.text: Answer number one bags mark for successful candidate

indicators.note: bags means captures or holds, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a 'number one' is a childish euphemism for a pee
a point is a dot or mark

explanation.surface: The answer is that the top candidate earns a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' is nursery slang for urinating, not a ranking; 'bags' means holds.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointee is the person given a post, the candidate who wins the selection.

clue.text: Part of tortoise arguably shell-like

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Debating whether a bit of a tortoise resembles a shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell-like' is a British jocular word for the ear, as in 'a word in your shell-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell-like is British slang for an ear, from the shell shape of the outer organ.

clue.text: Very enjoyable sandwich tasting, sharing one left

indicators.note: the two words overlap, sharing a single copy of the letter where they meet

parts.note: a roll is a bread roll, a sandwich
licking is tasting with the tongue

explanation.surface: A sandwich-tasting session where diners share one leftover portion is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: ROLL and LICKING overlap on one L, so a single L is dropped where they join.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollicking means exuberantly lively and fun, so a very enjoyable occasion.

clue.text: Fundaments with piles under underwear

indicators.note: in a down answer one word sits under the other

parts.note: bras are items of women's underwear
stacks are piles

explanation.surface: Bottoms, with heaps of laundry stacked beneath the undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fundaments' tempts one to read bottoms, but here it means basics.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the basic essentials of a matter.

clue.text: Derby traders perhaps smell cool pies after power cut

parts.note: BO is body odour
OK, like cool, means fine or acceptable

indicators.note: the word pies has its power symbol cut away

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Stallholders at a race meeting sniffing chilled pies after an electricity failure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race, where bookmakers take bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookies are bookmakers, who trade in bets at race meetings such as the Derby.

clue.text: Beauty exposed ugly affair

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer layer, the first and last letters

parts.note: its inner letters
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A beautiful person's unpleasant liaison is brought to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring beauty or attractiveness.

clue.text: Development of horns gave beetles …

indicators.note: development turns these letters into something new, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Growing horns gave beetles a striking new look, as the next clue continues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beetles' looks like the insects but is the verb: to beetle is to project or jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetling brow or cliff juts out, so to beetle is to project over, the same as to overhang.

clue.text: Metalworker putting gold in fruit recipe

indicators.note: in tells us one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
or is gold in heraldry
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A craftsman adds gold to a fruit recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorimer was a craftsman making bits, spurs and other small metal fittings for horses.

clue.text: … a rearing appearance, an improvement

indicators.note: rearing up, in a down answer, sets the word upside down so it is read backwards

parts.note: per means a or each, as in a pound per head
an air is an appearance or manner

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the beetles' horns give a rearing look, an enhancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is not just an article: it is PER, as in 'ten pounds a head', set upward to read REP.
explanation.definitionFit: A repair is a mending, fixing what is broken so it is better than before.

clue.text: Strange cycling, stones giving bumpy ride

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: odd means strange
gems are precious stones

explanation.surface: An unusual bike trip over rocks makes for an uncomfortable journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final D of ODD to the front, giving DOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgems are fairground bumper cars, which give a ride full of collisions.

clue.text: US marksman's bang I heard

parts.note: bang and dead both mean exactly, as in bang on or dead on

indicators.note: heard says the letter is taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter I is spoken like the word eye

explanation.surface: An American sharpshooter says he heard a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bang' looks like a gunshot, but means exactly: bang on is dead on.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadeye is American slang for an expert shot, a marksman who rarely misses.

clue.text: Heavy furniture silly men drop again, just missing me

indicators.note: silly suggests foolish disorder, so the letters are scrambled
the letters of me are left out of the scrambled pool

explanation.surface: Clumsy removal men drop it again, narrowly missing the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ME out of MEN DROP AGAIN to leave NDROPAGAIN, which 'silly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand piano is a large, very heavy instrument, notorious for difficult removals.

clue.text: Get up around noon to wash

indicators.note: around means one word wraps the other

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Waking at midday and then cleaning up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly with clean water.

clue.text: Stop time with it

parts.note: ho is an old call to halt, as in 'westward ho'

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt time and keep up with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot means fashionable or trendy, the same idea as being with it.

clue.text: Impale vampires as they sleep?

indicators.note: bats sleep hanging upside down, so in a down answer the word is inverted

parts.note: vampire bats, so bats

explanation.surface: A vampire-hunter's question about staking his victims while they slumber.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats roost upside down, which in a down entry means reading the word from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab is to pierce with a pointed weapon, as one impales on a stake.

clue.text: Figure drip in gallery is experimental

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure

indicators.note: in places one word within the other

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
IV is an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: A hospital patient on a drip at an art gallery is a bold trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries, here holding IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentative means provisional, done as a trial, so experimental.

clue.text: Consult on Iceland bagging pepper up

indicators.note: bagging means holding, so these words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Advice to ask the Iceland store for spicing up your shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something that invigorates or revives, a pick-me-up.

clue.text: Extra repeated line when exiting

indicators.note: repeated says the same word comes a second time, back to back

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball

explanation.surface: An extra repeated line in a script for leaving the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched, counted as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye-bye is the phrase people say as they leave, a farewell.

clue.text: Scratching Costner's back, Rene Russo treated psychological problems

indicators.note: scratching here means striking out, so that letter is left out of the pool
treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged
a name's back is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of Costner

explanation.surface: Rene Russo is treated for anxieties while scratching Kevin Costner's back, her co-star.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike R (Costner's back) out of RENE RUSSO and 'treated' rearranges ENEUSSOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuroses are mild mental disorders such as anxiety or obsession.
